question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186166865/plots/eb792727df2cbc0b40f05fb6.png)

Find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ for the circle shown above.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since our circle is centered at the origin and has a radius of $\sqrt{2},$ its equation is given by

$$
{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}={\sqrt{2}}^{2}\,⟹\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=2.
$$

Now, to calculate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use implicit differentiation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({y}^{2}) & =0 \\ 2x+2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =0 \\ 2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-2x \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{x}{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ for the circle shown above.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since our circle is centered at $(-1,-1)$ and has a radius of $3,$ its equation is given by

$$
(x-(-1))^{2}+(y-(-1))^{2}={3}^{2}\,⟹\,(x+1)^{2}+(y+1)^{2}=9.
$$

Now, to calculate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use implicit differentiation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}((x+1)^{2}+(y+1)^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(9) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}((x+1)^{2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}((y+1)^{2}) & =0 \\ 2(x+1)+2(y+1)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =0 \\ 2(y+1)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-2(x+1) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{x+1}{y+1}\end{aligned}
$$
